title: Slotized HW performance envelope and transient-throttle mapping for A100/H100/L40S/MI300
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current per-device performance profiles assume steady-state throughput/latency and ignore short-lived transient events (thermal throttles, power-capping on mixed racks, short-duration frequency scaling). These transients cause model pin recommendations to flip-flop and produce surprising tail latency regressions for customers during bursty workloads.

Goal: Produce a new artifact type — a 'slotized performance envelope' — that captures short (0-60s) and medium (1-10min) transient behavior per GPU SKU (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) across representative model families and batch size distributions. Publish these envelopes with metadata so the pin recommender and model-onboard workflow can account for transient risk and soft-fallback thresholds.

Scope and deliverables:
- Micro-benchmark harness that runs across target SKUs under controlled thermal and power cap conditions and produces slotized envelopes (0-10s, 10-60s, 1-10min).
- Data schema for envelope artifacts (sequence_length, batch_distribution_signature, slot_durations, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, energy_estimate, observed-frequency-drop, throttle-events).
- Integration point for onboarding: a new 'transient_risk_score' used by auto-pin logic and the onboarding checklist.
- Publication playbook: where and how envelopes are stored, versioned, and surfaced in Console and the model catalog (artifact links + human-readable summary).

Why different from existing profiles: Existing artifacts capture steady-state averages and 'signature' deltas. This ticket formalizes transient windows across a fixed slotization and ties them directly to pinning logic and release gating so we don't treat short thermal ramps as permanent regressions.

Trade-offs considered:
- More slots => higher fidelity vs. longer/expensive runs. Chosen compromise: three slot buckets (short/medium/long) to capture the majority of customer-observed incidents while keeping per-device benchmark time under 3 hours.
- Synthetic thermal/power injection vs. field telemetry: we'll start with controlled lab injections to create repeatable envelopes, then validate with sampled in-field traces to calibrate thresholds.
- Schema richness vs. consumption complexity: extra fields (energy, freq-drop) added but optional for downstream consumers; pin recommender uses simplified transient_risk_score to avoid complexity in runtime decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A harness exists that can produce slotized envelopes for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 within 3 hours per device variant.
Envelope artifact schema documented and stored in Confluence with examples for two sample models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder).
Pinned model onboarding flow is updated to read transient_risk_score and produce a recommended soft-pin with rollback policy.
Publishing playbook drafted and validated in an internal test: Console surfaces transient summaries on the model page and the PRD for release notes is updated.
